evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user need (creating a game) without prescribing specific UI widgets or implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: States the need to invite via a URL; does not mandate concrete UI elements or technical implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes a concrete UI widget (a single multi-line text field) rather than just the need to enter an item.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Focuses on the stakeholder need (visibility of items) without specifying solution details.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses required capability (selecting an item) without prescribing UI/technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the need to add items; does not dictate how it must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to edit items without prescribing a specific solution.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Captures the stakeholder need (removing an item) without implementation/UI prescription.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: States desired behavior (revealing estimates early) without specifying UI widgets or technical approach.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a business rule/need (use average) rather than an implementation mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific UI element/behavior (“estimate” field auto-filled) instead of stating the underlying need (speeding acceptance when unanimous).

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user need to record an agreed estimate without prescribing UI/technical details.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: States the need for re-estimation without specifying solution choices.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily constrains the solution to a specific source/format (“spreadsheet”) rather than the need to bulk import stories.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete mechanism (copy/paste) and specific source (spreadsheet) instead of the underlying need to quickly add multiple stories.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to find previous games without prescribing UI or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: States the need to view past content without specifying format/technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific storage/export format (HTML file) rather than the need to save/export transcripts.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific export/storage format (CSV) instead of the underlying need to export data for further processing.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need (remove a game and its data) without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Over-prescribes specific data fields as the solution rather than stating the need to create an account.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific authentication mechanism/credentials rather than the need to authenticate to access the application.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: States the need to update account information without prescribing UI/technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Captures the need to remove an account and associated data without specifying implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a user need (localized time display) without prescribing how to implement it.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific delivery mechanism (email) rather than the need to recover access when a password is forgotten.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a domain/business choice (which estimation scale to use) rather than UI/technical implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Over-prescribes a concrete limit (15) as a solution constraint rather than stating the need to support large teams.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific UI/context (“entering my name on the page” via URL) rather than the need to join a game.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: States the need for visibility of the current item without prescribing solution details.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to view the session backlog without implementation prescription.

evaluations.evidence: see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Describes the informational need (who has estimated) without specifying UI/technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: States desired behavior to preserve independence; does not prescribe concrete UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a capability/constraint on behavior without prescribing implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the need for historical visibility without prescribing how it is displayed or stored.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Describes the informational need without solution prescription.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific solution (a countdown timer) and a fixed duration (two-minute) rather than the underlying need to timebox discussion.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific mechanism (auto-reset timer) tied to a specific duration rather than the underlying need to prepare timing for the next round.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Mentions a UI interaction (“scroll back”) which is a concrete mechanism rather than just the need to review prior rounds.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: States a consistency requirement (stable ordering) without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to revise an estimate within a state constraint; no solution mechanism is mandated.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes concrete UI/visual design choices (“small thumbnail photo”, placement) rather than the need to personalize participants.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific technical standards/implementation choices (XHTML/CSS compliance) rather than the underlying accessibility/compatibility need.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: States the need for shared understanding; does not prescribe technical implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Directly prescribes an implementation detail (database indexes) instead of stating the performance need.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Over-prescribes specific technical targets (exact browser versions) rather than the general stakeholder need for broad compatibility.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific standard as the solution approach rather than stating the accessibility need in problem terms.

evaluations.evidence: application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: States a performance need without prescribing implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific technical mechanism/encoding (Unicode) rather than the underlying need to support multiple languages/characters.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a solution-level artifact (URL structure) rather than the underlying need (transparent navigation/shareability).

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific UI solution (“error pages”) rather than the underlying need (clear, trustworthy error handling/communication).

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: States a stakeholder need (non-identifiable storage for research/privacy) without prescribing specific technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need for usage metrics without prescribing how they are collected or displayed.
